title.big: Where does this well actually flow?
title.desc: Ask in plain English. Deckhand asks for what it needs, runs the calculation, and sends back a report you can keep.

turns.html: I want the operating point on one of my oil wells — where the inflow and the tubing lift balance out. Can you run a nodal analysis?

Happy to. I find the operating point where the inflow curve and the tubing-lift curve cross, so I need a bit on each side:
  • Inflow (IPR) — reservoir pressure and the well's productivity index? Bubble point too, if you have it.
  • Lift (VLP) — tubing size and depth, water cut, and gas-oil ratio?
  • Surface — the wellhead pressure you're flowing against, and fluid basics (oil gravity, temperature)?
I'll use a Vogel inflow curve since the well draws below bubble point. If it's gas or multi-layer, tell me and I'll flag it for a different method.
Reservoir 3,000 psi, productivity index 2.0 bopd/psi, bubble point 2,500 psi. Tubing is 2.992" ID at 8,000 ft, 20% water cut, GOR 400 scf/bbl. Wellhead 200 psi, 35° oil at 180°F. Details attached.

Got it. I'll build the Vogel inflow curve from your 3,000 psi reservoir pressure and 2.0 bopd/psi index, then the tubing-lift curve up the 2.992" string to the 200 psi wellhead, and find where they cross. Running it now…

Here's the operating point where inflow meets lift:

The well settles at about 997 bopd with 2,458 psi at the perforations — a 542 psi drawdown. Confidence is green on your test data.

report.title: Nodal Analysis (IPR/VLP)
report.inputs:
Reservoir (inflow)
IPR model — Vogel
Reservoir pressure 3,000 psi · Bubble point 2,500 psi
Productivity index 2.0 bopd/psi

Tubing (lift)
Depth 8,000 ft · ID 2.992"
Water cut 20% · GOR 400 scf/bbl

Surface & fluid
Wellhead pressure 200 psi · Temperature 180°F
Oil 35° · Gas gravity 0.65 · Test quality 85
report.methodology:
1 · Build the inflow (IPR) curve — Vogel relation from reservoir pressure and productivity index, drawing below bubble point.
2 · Build the tubing-lift (VLP) curve — pressure climb up the 2.992" string to the 200 psi wellhead, with water cut and gas-oil ratio.
3 · Find the operating point where the two curves cross — the rate the well actually delivers.
4 · Read off the flowing bottomhole pressure at the crossing and the drawdown.
5 · Band the rate by test quality to give a working range.
